title: The kept slides describe one service while this run delivers 19 services
source: 12 Project communication/Recovery Workbench Team Start Pack v2.pptx slides 2 and 3; Template and Rules v1 R4 and R5.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13 to 20
section: Slide 2 'What we are building'; slide 3 'Where the work happens in ACE'
description: Version 2 says the Recovery Workbench is built on ACE as 'one service, one repository and one front end', and slide 3 repeats it. The realignment delivers 19 services, 7 platform epics and 5 integration epics (U1, R5.1), with one schema, login, REST base, topic and Temporal task queue per service (R4). The work package keeps every line of the source, so the deck now carries both readings and does not say which one a new team should act on.
evidence: Slide 2: 'Built on ACE ... One service, one repository and one front end, with data through COLLINS'; slide 3: 'One service, one repository, one front end.'; Template and Rules R4 (19 services) and R5.1 (platform, service and integration epics).
proposed: Read the kept lines as the ACE module boundary: the Recovery Workbench is one module of ACE and 19 services inside it, and name the 19 services and their epics on the new slides without changing the kept wording in this version.

title: The first-items slide depends on two cancelled legacy keys and on a split key
source: 12 Project communication/Recovery Workbench Team Start Pack v2.pptx slide 12; Template and Rules v1 R6; _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json legacy
section: Slide 12 'The first items to pull', column Depends on
description: RWB-E1-007 depends on RWB-E1-001 and RWB-E1-004, RWB-E1-018 on RWB-E1-016 and RWB-E1-012, RWB-E1-019 on RWB-E1-012 and RWB-E1-038, RWB-E1-027 on RWB-E1-056, and RWB-E1-043 on RWB-E1-011. Under the realignment E1-004 and E1-012 are already cancelled and get no story, E1-013 and E1-008 are split into six slices each, and every other key on the slide is split too, with dependencies of its own. A team that pulls by the dependency column of the slide waits for keys that have no story.
evidence: Slide 12 rows RWB-E1-007 (RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-004), RWB-E1-018 (RWB-E1-016, RWB-E1-012), RWB-E1-019 (RWB-E1-012, RWB-E1-038); Template and Rules R6 'Already cancelled: E1-003, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 029, 048, 051; TE-005'; split_plan.json legacy has no entry for E1-004 or E1-012 and six slices for RWB-E1-013 and RWB-E1-008.
proposed: Keep the slide word for word and state that the dependency a team pulls is the one on its own story, read from the Day-1 Work Allocation v1 and the Service Story Catalog v1, where the cancelled keys do not appear.

title: The release table gives eight epic releases and no wave, and the allocation is by team type and wave
source: 12 Project communication/Recovery Workbench Team Start Pack v2.pptx slide 4; Template and Rules v1 R4, R5.6
section: Slide 4 'Eight monthly releases'; new slides 15 to 20
description: Slide 4 gives E1 to E8 with one release date each. The plan places every story in a wave 0 to 4 (R4 service table, R5.6 W-MAP) and tags it with a business epic EP01 to EP08, and the Day-1 allocation on slides 15 to 20 is by team type and contract group CG-W<wave>. The deck does not state that E1 to E8 are EP01 to EP08, or how an epic release relates to a wave, so a reader cannot place a wave 2 story on the release table.
evidence: Slide 4 rows 'E1 30 Nov 2026', 'E2 31 Dec 2026' through 'E8 30 Jun 2027'; Template and Rules R5.6 (EP01 wave 1; EP02 and EP03 wave 2; EP04 and EP05 wave 3; EP06, EP07 and EP08 wave 4; platform and NF wave 0); R4 service waves 1 to 4.
proposed: State that E1 to E8 are the business epics EP01 to EP08, one release each, and that the wave of a story comes from Rules R5.6 and the service table; keep the eight dates as issued and read them as tentative.

title: No source document gives the Day-1 story count per team type
source: 12 Project communication/Recovery Workbench Team Start Pack v2.pptx (no Day-1 concept); Template and Rules v1 R5.7; _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json stats; 11 Delivery and operations/Recovery Workbench Day-1 Work Allocation v1.xlsx
section: New slide 15 'Day-1 work by team type'
description: The counts on slide 15 are 846 for TechX, 11 for the ACE team, 18 for SCB IT infrastructure, 57 for the DevOps team and 7 for the QA team, 939 in all of the 1034 stories of the plan. They are taken from the assembled Day-1 Work Allocation v1 and from the plan stats (day1 939, 1034 slices, five Day-1 teams). No source document of the programme states a count per team type, so the figures are run material and not a stated target or a capacity commitment.
evidence: split_plan.json stats: slices 1034, legacy 358, day1 939, day1_teams ACE, DEVOPS, INFRA, QA, TechX, lanes 510; Day-1 Work Allocation v1 sheets TechX 846, ACE 11, INFRA 18, DEVOPS 57, QA 7; version 2 slides 1 to 13 name no team type and no Day-1 count.
proposed: Publish the counts with their source (the Day-1 Work Allocation v1) and state that they measure the dependency graph of the plan and are not a commitment of capacity per team type.

title: The deck names no team type, and the suggested-owner phrase has no anchor in it
source: 12 Project communication/Recovery Workbench Team Start Pack v2.pptx slides 2 to 13; Template and Rules v1 R5.3
description: R5.3 fixes six work types with a suggested owner phrase of the form 'suggested; any team may pick up this story': TechX for CON and APP, the ACE team for DB, SCB IT infrastructure for INF, the DevOps team for OPS, and TechX with the QA team for ITG harness and NFR stories. The deck speaks of squads and modules ('Collection squad', 'TechX recovery squads') and names no team type, so the phrase is introduced by this version and is not anchored in the source.
evidence: Slide 3 rows 'Collection squad' and 'TechX recovery squads'; no slide of version 2 names a team type or the phrase 'suggested; any team may pick up this story'; Template and Rules R5.3.
proposed: Take the five team types from Rules R5.3 and the plan, and repeat the suggested-only phrase wherever an owner is named in this pack.

title: The deck has no Day-1, lane or contract-group concept
source: 12 Project communication/Recovery Workbench Team Start Pack v2.pptx slides 6 to 12; Template and Rules v1 R5.7
description: Slides 6 to 8 describe the flow, the rhythm and the gates, and slide 12 names the first items to pull. None of them says that a contract story is always Day 1, that a story whose only build edges are contract stories is Day 1, or that a lane is a group of non-contract stories linked by H dependencies with a depth of at most 4. The new slides 15 to 19 carry that reading and the kept slides do not.
evidence: Version 2 slides 6 to 12; Template and Rules R5.7 rules 1 to 8; R5.5 DP-11 (contract with a mock, one hop, 2 s timeout).
proposed: Add the Day-1 rule, the contract group and the lane to the pack as new slides, leave the kept slides unchanged, and point the reader to the Day-1 Work Allocation v1 for the full list.

title: The first-month tables plan by role and by week, and the allocation is by team type and by flow
source: 12 Project communication/Recovery Workbench Team Start Pack v2.pptx slides 10 and 11; Template and Rules v1 R5.3 and R5.7
section: Slides 10 and 11 'The first month'; new slides 18 and 20
description: Slides 10 and 11 give nine roles across four weeks (2 to 6 Nov, 9 to 13 Nov, 16 to 20 Nov and 23 to 27 Nov) with the work of each role in each week. The realignment plans by team type and by the pull from the board, and no source states which team type fills each role: product owner, business analysts, tech leads, developers, QA engineers, business testers, reference data administrator, data steward and release owner in the ACE team.
evidence: Slide 10 rows 'Product owner', 'Business analysts', 'Tech leads', 'Developers', 'QA engineers'; slide 11 rows 'Business testers', 'Reference data administrator', 'Data steward', 'Release owner, ACE team'; Template and Rules R5.3 (team types) and R5.7 rule 6.
proposed: Read each role as the team type that fills it, keep the four weeks as issued, and state the reading in the pack without changing the tables.

title: The Epic 1 and Epic 2 slide says 13 technical enabler stories, and the platform adds 12 stories, 8 NF stories and an integration harness
source: 12 Project communication/Recovery Workbench Team Start Pack v2.pptx slide 5; Template and Rules v1 R5.1 and R5.7 rule 6; _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json legacy
section: Slide 5 'Epic 1 and Epic 2', note under the table; new slide 17
description: Slide 5 says '13 technical enabler stories run alongside, and three agent stories carry into Epic 3'. The realignment adds 12 platform stories N001 to N012, keeps the eight NF stories NF-01 to NF-08 and adds the integration harness W1J01 and W1J02, and these are the Day-1 work of the ACE team, SCB IT infrastructure, the DevOps team and the QA team (R5.7 rule 6). A reader of slide 5 alone sees 13 enablers and no platform or harness work.
evidence: Slide 5 note; Template and Rules R5.7 rule 6 ('The new platform stories N001-N012 and the integration harness W1J01 make sure of this'); split_plan.json legacy lists N001 to N012, NF-01 to NF-08, W1J01 and W1J02.
proposed: Keep the 13 enabler stories as issued and name the 12 platform stories, the 8 NF stories and the harness as added work on the new slides, each with its team type.
